# Micro QR Spec-to-Code Map (ISO/IEC 18004)

This document maps each part of the Micro QR specification (ISO/IEC 18004, versions M1-M4) to its implementation. The decoder's scope, decisions and lessons are in the [design record](microqr-decoder.md). [QR Symbology Architecture](qrcode-symbologies.md) describes the document set and the shared and per-symbology components.

It is a map, not a copy of the spec. Normative details (bit layouts, formulas, edge-case constraints) and the reasons for implementation choices are in code comments next to the implementation, where they stay in sync with the code.

## Encoding Pipeline Overview

```
Text ──> Mode analysis ──> Data encoding ──> ECC ──> Module placement ──> Masking ──> Format info
```

Micro QR has a single Reed-Solomon block and no codeword interleaving, so it has no counterpart to the Standard QR interleaving stage.

## Decoding Pipeline Overview (matrix level)

```
Module matrix ──> core located ──> version from size ──> format information ──> codeword extraction and unmasking
              ──> Reed-Solomon correction ──> bitstream decode ──> text
```

The matrix level has the same internal boundary as the Standard QR `QRMatrixDecoder`. The public entry, [MicroQRCodeDecoder](../../../src/FeatherQR/MicroQRCodeDecoder.cs), takes `MicroQRCodeData`, a module matrix or a zero-allocation span and strips a uniform quiet zone. Its image overloads are listed below. Diagnostics are in [MicroQRCodeDecodeInfo](../../../src/FeatherQR/MicroQRCodeDecodeInfo.cs).

| Spec reference | Topic | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| - | Core located: a module span may include a light quiet zone. The top-left dark module is the finder's corner. The core size assumes a uniform border, because the right and bottom edges carry data and need not be dark. `MicroQRCodeData` input is already the core | [MicroQRCodeDecoder.TryLocateCore](../../../src/FeatherQR/MicroQRCodeDecoder.cs) |
| - | Version from size (11/13/15/17), then the stages below in order. With a single RS block there is no deinterleaving | [MicroQRMatrixDecoder](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRMatrixDecoder.cs) |
| - | Format information decode: the symbol's single 15-bit copy is matched against all 32 valid patterns, correcting up to 3 bit errors (BCH(15,5), minimum distance 7), and its version must match the physical matrix size. A 32 KB table maps every 15-bit word within 3 bits of a candidate to that candidate. The candidates' balls never overlap, so one lookup is the whole search. This matters on a failing image, where the image searches decode hundreds of thousands of grids | [MicroQRFormatInformationDecoder](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRFormatInformationDecoder.cs), cross-check in [MicroQRMatrixDecoder](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRMatrixDecoder.cs) |
| Section 7.7.3 | Codeword extraction and unmasking: the inverse zigzag unmasks as it reads, through a per-size placement table built from the encoder's own `IsFunctionModule` / `GetMaskBit`, so encoder and decoder always agree. The grid is read through a view, which the image decoder transposes for a mirrored capture instead of copying the grid transposed | [MicroQRMatrixDecoder.ExtractCodewords](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRMatrixDecoder.cs) |
| Section 8.5 | Reed-Solomon correction | [EccBinaryDecoder](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/BinaryDecoders/EccBinaryDecoder.cs), shared across symbologies |
| Table 9 | Error correction capacity t, where 2t + p = ecc codewords (p=2 on detection-only M1, p=3 on M2-L and p=2 on M2-M/M3-L/M4-L). The decoder must reject corrections beyond t, even where Reed-Solomon could correct more | [MicroQRConstants.GetErrorCorrectionCapacity](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRConstants.cs), enforced in [MicroQRMatrixDecoder](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRMatrixDecoder.cs) |
| Table 2/3 | Bitstream decode: a mode indicator of version − 1 bits (none on M1, which is implicitly Numeric), then the count indicators. The terminator is Numeric mode with a zero count, possibly truncated at capacity. The bit capacity bounds the stream and ends in a half codeword on M1/M3. Kanji (M3/M4) is decoded through the shared JIS X 0208 table | [MicroQRBinaryDecoder](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRBinaryDecoder.cs) |
| Section 7.4.3-7.4.5 | Segment payload decoding, shared with the Standard QR decoder: numeric in 10/7/4-bit groups, alphanumeric in 11/6-bit groups, and byte with a UTF-8 / Shift_JIS / Latin-1 heuristic | [SegmentDecoders](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/BinaryDecoders/SegmentDecoders.cs) |

Reference tests: [MicroQRFormatInformationDecoderUnitTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/MicroQR/MicroQRFormatInformationDecoderUnitTest.cs) (every word of the 15-bit space against a naive nearest-candidate reference, and the ISO Table 9 capacities), [MicroQRMatrixDecoderExtractParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/MicroQR/MicroQRMatrixDecoderExtractParityTest.cs) (codeword extraction against a per-module zigzag walk that reads no placement table, byte for byte, for every version and level, mask, grid shape and both module views), [MicroQRBinaryDecoderUnitTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/MicroQR/MicroQRBinaryDecoderUnitTest.cs) (M1 golden vectors, the ISO "01234567" M2-L example, encoder round trips, malformed-stream negatives), [MicroQRCodeDecoderRoundTripTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/MicroQR/MicroQRCodeDecoderRoundTripTest.cs) (all versions × ECC × modes, quiet zones, span parity), [MicroQRCodeDecoderRobustnessTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/MicroQR/MicroQRCodeDecoderRobustnessTest.cs) (damage per equivalence class: within t, the t&lt;errors≤⌊ecc/2⌋ misdecode guard, beyond RS range, M1 detection-only, format damage, cross-symbology rejection), [MicroQRFixtureTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/MicroQR/MicroQRFixtureTest.cs) (committed external-encoder corpus, two lineages).

| Spec reference | Topic | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| Section 7.4.1 | Mode detection (Numeric / Alphanumeric / Byte) | [TextAnalyzer.Analyze](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/TextAnalyzer.cs), shared across symbologies |
| Table 2 | Mode indicator widths (M1: none, M2-M4: version − 1 bits) and values | [MicroQRConstants.GetModeIndicatorLength / GetModeIndicatorValue](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRConstants.cs) |
| Table 3 | Character count indicator widths (Numeric = version + 2, Alphanumeric/Byte = version + 1, Kanji = version on M3/M4) | [MicroQRConstants.GetCountIndicatorLength](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRConstants.cs) |
| Section 7.4.3-7.4.5 | Numeric / Alphanumeric / Byte segment bit streams, written through a 128-bit accumulator. Byte mode uses platform-specific SIMD fast paths with a scalar fallback | [MicroQRBinaryEncoder](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRBinaryEncoder.cs) |
| Table 2 | Terminator of 3/5/7/9 zero bits, shortened at capacity, and pad codewords 0xEC/0x11. The final 4-bit pad is 0000 | [MicroQRBinaryEncoder.EncodeDataCodewords](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRBinaryEncoder.cs) |
| - | Mode availability per version for encoding (M1: Numeric, M2: +Alphanumeric, M3/M4: +Byte and Kanji). Both the single-segment and segmented encoders write Kanji. With `AllowKanji`, the generator selects Kanji for text whose every character has an encoder cell ([When Kanji mode is written](qrcode-symbologies.md#when-kanji-mode-is-written)) and, under `Optimal`, for the Kanji runs of a Kanji-eligible text's plan at M3 and M4 | [MicroQRConstants.IsModeSupported](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRConstants.cs). [MicroQRBinaryEncoderKanjiTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/MicroQR/MicroQRBinaryEncoderKanjiTest.cs) checks the writers against a reference built from the standard and the capacity against Table 7's Kanji column, and runs round trips |
| Section 7.4 (segment sequence) | Several segments in one symbol, each with its own mode and count indicator | [MicroQRSegmentPlanner](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRSegmentPlanner.cs) and [MicroQRBinaryEncoder.EncodeDataCodewordsSegmented](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRBinaryEncoder.Segmented.cs). The planner, opt-in through the public [MicroQRSegmentation](../../../src/FeatherQR/MicroQRSegmentation.cs), finds the split with the fewest bits. It also runs the version scan and handles each version's available modes. The cost model is [ModeSegmenter](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ModeSegmenter.cs), shared with Standard QR and rMQR. A plan that the ECI-less charset heuristics would misread (a Latin-1 run that reads as UTF-8 or Shift_JIS once isolated) is rejected in favour of the single-mode stream. The shared program opens no Byte run at a U+FEFF in mid-content, because a reader would drop it as a byte order mark. With `AllowKanji`, a Kanji-eligible text containing ASCII also gets a Kanji plan (Kanji runs beside runs of its ASCII) from the program's eighth state. Where it fits at a candidate version, the Kanji plan is taken ahead of the UTF-8 plan, and it is built by walking back the cost run that accepted it. The rationale is in [Standard QR Encoder](standardqr-encoder.md#mixed-mode-segmentation) |

Reference tests: [MicroQRSegmentPlannerUnitTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/MicroQR/MicroQRSegmentPlannerUnitTest.cs) (the planner's optimum against an independent exhaustive mode assignment within each version's mode set, the 35-character bound with its margin, and an expected three-run plan), [MicroQRSegmentationTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/MicroQR/MicroQRSegmentationTest.cs) (end to end: never a larger version than single mode, always decodes, byte-identical to single mode when the version does not change, the M2-without-Byte win, the no-single-mode rescue, and the requested-version / mask / precedence branches), [MicroQRBinaryEncoderUnitTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/MicroQR/MicroQRBinaryEncoderUnitTest.cs) (M1 golden vectors, the ISO "01234567" M2-L example, naive bit-string references for alphanumeric/byte/half-codeword padding), [MicroQRBinaryEncoderParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/MicroQR/MicroQRBinaryEncoderParityTest.cs) (the optimized encoder against an independent naive reference across all 8 version/ECC combinations, every supported mode and length, the full Latin-1 range, UTF-8 fallbacks including surrogate-pair / lone-surrogate handling, and a single non-Latin-1 char at every position of every length, which each SIMD tier's overlapped-window Latin-1 detector must see), [MicroQRBitAccumulatorUnitTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/MicroQR/MicroQRBitAccumulatorUnitTest.cs) (Append / Append64 / AppendWide boundary positions against an independent bit-string reference).

## Capacity and Symbol Tables

| Spec reference | Topic | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| Table 7 | Data capacity in bits for each version and ECC level (M1/M3 end on a 4-bit half codeword) | [MicroQRConstants.dataBitCapacities](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRConstants.cs) |
| Table 9 | Data / ECC codeword counts (single block, no interleaving) | [MicroQRConstants.dataCodewordCounts / eccCodewordCounts](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRConstants.cs) |
| - | Version/ECC legality (M1 is detection only, M2/M3 take L and M, and M4 takes L, M and Q) and smallest-version auto-selection | [MicroQRConstants.IsValidCombination](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRConstants.cs). [MicroQRCodeGenerator.TrySelectVersion](../../../src/FeatherQR/MicroQRCodeGenerator.cs) is the automatic fit. The text-span `PrepareConfiguration` wraps it and `NotFittingError` builds the message. A pinned version is fitted as a one-version range by `TrySelectVersionInRange` (next row), and the configuration is then built from that fit without checking the version again. The fits throw for an undefined ECC level, or a range that offers the level nowhere, before they can report failure, because those errors hold of the arguments whatever the text, and `false` means only that the content does not fit. An undefined version never reaches them, since `MicroQRVersionRange` rejects it when built. Bits are counted as `long`, so an oversized Byte payload's bit count cannot wrap into a false fit. The public form is `TryGetRequiredBufferSize` (contract in [rmqr-encoder.md](rmqr-encoder.md)). Here `false` also covers a mode the version or ECC level does not offer, because the text picks the mode |
| - | Version range selection (`MicroQRVersionRange`): the smallest version inside `[Min, Max]` that holds the content | [MicroQRCodeGenerator.TrySelectVersionInRange](../../../src/FeatherQR/MicroQRCodeGenerator.cs). When a range rules out every version, the reason decides the result. If no version in it offers the requested ECC level, the request is a contradiction no content could satisfy, so the call throws, a pinned version that does not offer the level included. If versions are available but none carries the mode the text requires or holds the content, the content does not fit and the call returns `false`, because the text picks the mode. `Create` then throws an error that names the narrowed range and looks only at its versions: the largest of them and what it holds, or the mode none of them carries at that level. It used to offer the largest version of all, which could lie outside the range the caller set. `MicroQRVersionRange.Any` goes straight to the existing automatic path, whose messages are unchanged, as are a pinned version's |

Reference tests: [MicroQRConstantsUnitTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/MicroQR/MicroQRConstantsUnitTest.cs) (table values), [MicroQRCodeGeneratorUnitTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/MicroQR/MicroQRCodeGeneratorUnitTest.cs) (capacity boundaries per mode × ECC, illegal-combination rejection), [TryGetRequiredBufferSizeTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/TryGetRequiredBufferSizeTest.cs) (`Try` reports the size the encode then fills, over content × ECC × requested version. Through 1.2.0 it checked agreement with the released throwing `Get`, and it was re-pointed at the encode before 2.0.0 removed that overload), [VersionRangeTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/VersionRangeTest.cs) (`Any` and `Exactly` reproduce the released automatic and pinned behaviour byte for byte. It also checks the split above between an ECC contradiction and a mode exclusion, and the exact error a narrowed range that does not fit reports on every entry point and both segmentations), [CapacityOverflowGuardTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/CapacityOverflowGuardTest.cs) (a length that wraps the bit count around is rejected, and argument errors still throw at that length), [ResolvedEncodeOutputTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/ResolvedEncodeOutputTest.cs) (pinned and ranged encodes, and the mixed-mode encodes that write the single-mode stream, frozen as hashes and exact error messages: the analysis that picks the version is the one the symbol is written from, Kanji and Kanji-plannable text included).

| Spec reference | Topic | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| Section 6.3 | Single finder pattern, separators, edge timing patterns (row 0 / column 0) | [MicroQRModulePlacer.PlaceFunctionModules](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRModulePlacer.cs) |
| - | Function region predicate: `row == 0 ‖ col == 0 ‖ (row ≤ 8 ∧ col ≤ 8)` | [MicroQRModulePlacer.IsFunctionModule](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRModulePlacer.cs) |

BMI2+AVX2 does the placement as a static per-row PEXT/PDEP permutation and runs only on hardware with fast PEXT (Intel or AMD Zen 3+). The per-module methods above remain as the readable reference | [MicroQRModulePlacer.PlaceSymbol](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRModulePlacer.PlaceSymbol.cs) |
| - | Output: every tier writes every module of the core, so no caller clears it. The span output with a quiet zone has the placer write the centered window directly, rows a destination row apart, and clears only the margins, before the placer, as rMQR does: the vector tiers' row unpack may run past a row into the margins, but only with light modules (`QuietZoneWindow` in [QR Symbology Architecture](qrcode-symbologies.md)) | [MicroQRCodeGenerator.Create](../../../src/FeatherQR/MicroQRCodeGenerator.cs), [MicroQRModulePlacer.PlaceSymbol](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRModulePlacer.PlaceSymbol.cs) (strided), [QuietZoneWindow.ClearMargins](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/QuietZoneWindow.cs) |

## Image Detection and Sampling

Each scan of the [shared image decode passes](qrcode-symbologies.md#image-decode-passes) runs this path on its ranked finder candidates. The passes and the scans are drawn in that section.

```
Ranked finder candidates: the scan's most confirmed first
└─ Each candidate
   ├─ Module sizes and centre
   ├─ Axis-aligned path, each right-angle orientation
   │  ├─ Each size, M4 down to M1: affine grid ──> matrix decode; coverage re-read (grey levels) ──> matrix decode
   │  ├─ Timing frame: the grid fitted to the timing patterns ──> matrix decode
   │  └─ Low density: module boundaries read off the timing patterns ──> matrix decode
   └─ Arbitrary orientation: each axis frame from an angular sweep, each right-angle orientation,
      within an attempt budget
      └─ Each size, M4 down to M1: affine grid ──> matrix decode; coverage re-read (grey levels) ──> matrix decode
         └─ Once a grid gets past its format information: scale search, then perspective search,
            each grid ──> matrix decode; coverage re-read (grey levels) ──> matrix decode

Matrix decode: the grid through the matrix level from version from size on, keeping only the corrections its
structure earns (grid evidence); then, unless it read (a read that did not fit included), the grid transposed (mirror)
A read ends the scan; one too long for the destination ends its candidate, and the scan once the other candidates
of its finder scan have run (the shared candidate scan: qrcode-symbologies.md, single-finder candidate scan)
```

| Spec reference | Topic | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| - | Passes ([Image decode passes](qrcode-symbologies.md#image-decode-passes)). The inverted pass inverts the image with the shared [LuminanceInverter](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/LuminanceInverter.cs) | [ImageDecodePasses](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/ImageDecodePasses.cs), shared across symbologies, over [MicroQRImageDecoder.SymbolPass](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRImageDecoder.cs). [ImageDecodePassesTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/ImageDecodePassesTest.cs) tests the passes |
| - | Global threshold (Otsu), shared with Standard QR. It moved to `Internals.ImageDecoders` when Micro QR became its second consumer. The histogram covers the whole buffer without a stride. It also gives the grey levels of the two classes it separates and, mirrored, the inverted retry's threshold and grey levels | [Binarizer.FillHistogram, ComputeOtsuThresholdFromHistogram](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/Binarizer.cs) |
| - | Regional binarization, used when neither polarity of the global threshold reads anything or gives a verdict on the content. Each pixel is compared with the mean black point of the 5 × 5 blocks around its 8 × 8 block. It runs on the positive, then on the negative, each from its own pixels, and each result is decoded only when it moves a pixel out of the class that polarity's global threshold gave it. An image of only 0 and 255, or with a side of 32 px or less, is not binarized. It is shared across symbologies, with a 128-bit tier for its three passes. Each attempt runs the decoder's own finder search, as for the global threshold (for Micro QR and rMQR, a strided scan, then a full sweep when nothing was read) | [LocalBinarizer](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/LocalBinarizer.cs), [RegionalRetry](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/RegionalRetry.cs). Parity: [LocalBinarizerParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/LocalBinarizerParityTest.cs). Retry: [RegionalRetryTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/RegionalRetryTest.cs). Decode: [UnevenLightingDecodeTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/UnevenLightingDecodeTest.cs) |
| Section 6.3.1 | Ranked finder candidates: the [shared candidate scan](qrcode-symbologies.md#single-finder-candidate-scan) tries the first eight, most confirmed first. A read ends the scan. A read too long for the destination ends its candidate and skips the candidates inside that symbol. Otherwise each finder scan reports the result that went furthest, and the scan reports the sweep's result if it settled, else the strided scan's. The candidates come from the shared 1:1:3:1:1 run scan, which collects every cross-checked candidate (Standard QR keeps its best-three selection) and moved to `Internals.ImageDecoders` when Micro QR became its second consumer. Since the rMQR follow-up the run scan is row-strided, and the image decoders re-run the sweep without a stride when nothing was read (a read too long for the destination counts), so on a single-symbol image the detection envelope is never narrower than a full sweep's. The sweep skips a candidate equal to one the strided scan decoded, since it would decode the same way, unless that scan ended in a verdict on the content. Runs that miss the ratio by about a pixel are measured again from the grey levels before refusal, so anti-aliased edges at about 2 px/module read. Each cross-check line must match the ratio on its own, and a column may be as far from its row as perspective draws a finder. A ring printed or read thick or thin is read by the distances between its like edges ([shared finder check](qrcode-symbologies.md#internal-organization)) | [FinderPatternFinder.FindCandidates, RankByConfirmation](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/FinderPatternFinder.cs), shared across symbologies. The candidate: [MicroQRImageDecoder.DecodeCandidate, DecodeBothWays](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRImageDecoder.cs). The first eight, the skip and the result: [CandidateScan](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/CandidateScan.cs) over [SearchResult](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/SearchResult.cs) (`ReportRule.Furthest`), shared across symbologies. The rules: [SearchResultTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/SearchResultTest.cs), [CandidateScanTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/CandidateScanTest.cs). A candidate inside the symbol that read: [SymbolGeometry.AnyContains](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/SymbolGeometry.cs), shared across symbologies. A read that does not fit: [DestinationContractTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/DestinationContractTest.cs), [SymbolGeometryContainsTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/SymbolGeometryContainsTest.cs) |
| - | Module sizes and centre: the horizontal and vertical module sizes come from dark-light-dark runs through the finder centre, each pairing the dark ring's inner edge on one side with its outer edge on the other, six modules apart. A candidate under one pixel per module is dropped. On an image with grey levels, the centre moves to the centroid of its centre square's darkness | [FinderAxisEstimator.RefineModuleSize](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/FinderAxisEstimator.cs), [ConcentricCentroid](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/ConcentricCentroid.cs), shared across symbologies |
| - | Axis-aligned path: in each right-angle orientation, for each size from M4 down to M1, a grid with the two module sizes is anchored on the finder centre at (3.5, 3.5) and skipped if it does not fit the image. The affine module-centre sampler samples it. Its 128-bit tier returns the same pixels as the scalar code, lane for lane | [MicroQRImageDecoder.DecodeCandidate, SampleGrid](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRImageDecoder.cs) |
| - | Coverage re-read: on an image with grey levels, a grid is read again when it neither read nor read too long for the destination, and one of its orientations got past its format information with that word read exactly. The re-read interpolates each module's luminance at its centre and splits it halfway between the two levels, and the grid is decoded again, in both orientations, only when that changes a module. It follows each size's grid in both paths and each grid of both searches, but not the timing frame or the module-boundary table | [GridRead](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/GridRead.cs), [LuminanceSampler](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/LuminanceSampler.cs), shared across symbologies. The exact-word gate: [MicroQRImageDecoder.BothWays](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRImageDecoder.cs). The gate and which decode is returned: [GridReadTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/GridReadTest.cs). A read that does not fit is not read again: [DestinationContractTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/DestinationContractTest.cs) |
| - | Timing frame: after an orientation's sizes, the grid is fitted by least squares to every module boundary along row 0 and column 0, from the finder's outer edge to the symbol's far edge, rather than extrapolated from the finder's module size. The dark runs give the size | [MicroQRImageDecoder.TryTimingFrame](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRImageDecoder.cs) |
| - | Low density: in an orientation whose larger module size is under 1.75 px, the grid is a table of module boundaries along row 0 and column 0 instead of a fitted grid. It needs both lines to read as timing patterns of the same size | [MicroQRImageDecoder.TryReadModuleBoundaries](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRImageDecoder.cs), [ModuleBoundaryReader](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/ModuleBoundaryReader.cs), shared across symbologies. Decode: [ModuleBoundaryReaderTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/ModuleBoundaryReaderTest.cs) (`MicroQR_CrispTurnedOrMirrored_Decodes`). Crisp M2-M4 renders between 1 and 1.5 px/module: [FractionalLowDensityDecodeTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/FractionalLowDensityDecodeTest.cs) |
| - | Arbitrary orientation: after the axis-aligned path, an angular sweep recovers the finder's local axes (an axis fitted over the sweep, then its separated minima, up to sixteen frames), and each frame's centre is refined along its own axes. Each right-angle orientation and each size from M4 down to M1 is then tried as in the axis-aligned path, within a per-candidate budget of sampled-grid decodes that excludes coverage re-reads. Every grid spends two decodes, one per orientation, so the budget ends the path between grids | [MicroQRImageDecoder.TryDecodeArbitraryOrientation](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRImageDecoder.cs), [FinderAxisEstimator.FindOrientationCandidates](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/FinderAxisEstimator.cs), shared with rMQR |
| - | Scale search: once an affine grid of the arbitrary-orientation path gets past its format information in either orientation, the search moves the centre by half a pixel and changes each axis's module size by a few percent | [MicroQRImageDecoder.TryDecodeScaleVariants](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRImageDecoder.cs) |
| - | Perspective search: next, the search tries a small grid of mild values for the two projective coefficients a single finder leaves unknown. Each grid is sampled through the projective transform and the square-grid sampler | [MicroQRImageDecoder.TryDecodePerspectiveVariants](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRImageDecoder.cs), [PerspectiveTransform.FromLocalFrame](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/PerspectiveTransform.cs), [PerspectiveGridSampler](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/PerspectiveGridSampler.cs), shared with Standard QR. Parity of the sampler's tiers, at Micro QR's sizes too: [PerspectiveGridSamplerParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/PerspectiveGridSamplerParityTest.cs) |
| - | Matrix decode and grid evidence: each sampled grid goes through the matrix level from version from size on and, unless it read (a read that did not fit counts), again transposed. A grid keeps only the corrections its structure supports. The evidence is Reed-Solomon's strength at the correction count, the format word's distance, the timing modules and, when those fall short, the quiet-zone modules along the right and bottom edges, summed in bits. The sum must reach 33. So M1, which corrects nothing, is never kept on its format word and timing alone. The evidence is counted after Reed-Solomon has corrected the grid, and a read beyond what the grid supports fails like a correction failure. The same rule applies in every pass, in place of refusals by level | [MicroQRGridEvidence](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRGridEvidence.cs), [MicroQRMatrixDecoder.DecodeSampledGrid](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRMatrixDecoder.cs), [MicroQRQuietZone](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/MicroQR/MicroQRQuietZone.cs). Rule: [MicroQRGridEvidenceTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/MicroQR/MicroQRGridEvidenceTest.cs). Decode: [UnevenLightingDecodeTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/UnevenLightingDecodeTest.cs) |
| - | Public image entry points (SKBitmap / luminance span / zero-allocation destination) | [MicroQRCodeImageDecoder.TryDecode(SKBitmap, …)](../../../src/FeatherQR.SkiaSharp/MicroQRCodeImageDecoder.cs) (rendering package) / [MicroQRCodeDecoder.TryDecodeImage](../../../src/FeatherQR/MicroQRCodeDecoder.cs) (core) |

The supported envelope, its measurements and the reasons for its limits are in the [design record](microqr-decoder.md#supported).

## Maintenance Notes

- When adding or moving a spec-referenced implementation, update this map. Keep details (bit layouts, formulas, constraints) in the code comment next to the implementation, not here.
- [MicroQRMatrixExtractionTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/MicroQR/MicroQRMatrixExtractionTest.cs) stays as an encoder-side consistency check with its own extraction code. It predates the decoder and does not depend on it. External-encoder fixtures and the oracle matrix are tracked in the [fixture record](qrcode-test-fixtures.md).
- Components marked "shared across symbologies" live outside `Internals/MicroQR`. The split is defined in [QR Symbology Architecture](qrcode-symbologies.md).
- A change that adds, removes or reorders a decode stage or retry also updates this map's decode diagrams, the image decoder's pipeline remarks and the decode figures in the [design record](microqr-decoder.md#image-decode-figures). For the figures, rerun `dotnet run tools/decode_figures.cs -- .github/docs/images`, then recheck each figure's box states and notes against the code. A change inside a stage, such as a tolerance or a gate, can also flip a box's state, and the tool checks the decodes, not the box states.
